elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: The proviso expressly permits either party, including Customer, to assign the Agreement to an affiliate without consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: The merger carve-out remains subject to consent when the transaction involves a direct competitor of Vendor, so Customer's right is not unconditional.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The acquisition carve-out remains subject to consent when the transaction involves a direct competitor of Vendor, so Customer's right is not unconditional.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The clause requires consent for transactions involving a direct competitor and limits the sale carve-out to assets 'related to this Agreement,' which is narrower than substantially all assets generally.

elements.element: Vendor must obtain Customer's consent for any assignment.
elements.evidence: Vendor may assign without consent to an affiliate and in qualifying merger, acquisition, or asset-sale transactions.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Vendor assignment.
elements.evidence: The clause provides that required consent may not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign this Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: A transaction involving a direct competitor merely requires consent rather than being prohibited, and the affiliate carve-out may also permit assignment to a competitor affiliate without consent.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right arising from Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause grants no termination right upon Customer's change of control.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Customer's transaction assignment right is subject to consent when the successor transaction involves a direct competitor of Vendor.

elements.element: Customer must give Vendor written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no written-notice requirement for successor assignments.

elements.element: Vendor may assign this Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Vendor's transaction assignment right is subject to consent when the successor transaction involves a direct competitor of Customer.

elements.element: Vendor must give Customer written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no written-notice requirement for successor assignments.

elements.element: Vendor's consent is required for Customer assignments other than successor assignments.
elements.evidence: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent even where the affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to Customer assignments for which consent is required.
elements.evidence: The clause provides that required consent may not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.

elements.element: Customer's consent is required for Vendor assignments other than successor assignments.
elements.evidence: Vendor may assign to an affiliate without consent even where the affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to Vendor assignments for which consent is required.
elements.evidence: The clause provides that required consent may not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.

result.reason: The redline is generally coherent but reaches neither position. It makes the affiliate carve-out mutual, preserves consent-based competitor exceptions instead of absolutely prohibiting Vendor assignments to Customer competitors, and omits the fallback's written-notice duties. It also permits non-successor affiliate assignments without consent, contrary to the fallback. The remaining provisions are operative and no unrelated commercial term is displaced.
